newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.00/3.03 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.00/3.03 percent.

text.p: German call money rates were steady at around 3.00 percent on Tuesday after the Bundesbank said it had added 1.1 billion marks to the market.

Traders said the cash injection, which was slightly higher than expected, was probably made to counter a small decline in commercial bank's reserve deposits, which fell to 40.3 billion marks on Monday from 41.3 billion marks on Friday.

"The Bundesbank is well aware of what it has to calculate," said one trader. "One billion marks already flowed out yesterday, and if there are more cash outflows today and tomorrow, then reserve levels will come off a bit."

The central bank said it had allocated 61.0 billion marks in securities repurchase funds at 3.0 percent, while a repo pact for 59.9 billion marks, also at 3.00 percent, expires this session, leaving a net 1.1 billion mark inflow.
The monthly average of deposits held at the Bundesbank stood at 41.1. billion marks on Monday, a little lower than Friday's 41.3 billion level.

Borrowing on the Lombard facility totalled around 0.1 billion marks, while the Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) rate was quoted at around 3.0700 in midday dealings on Tuesday. -- Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 7565 1246
